input: Apply for a sabbatical leave from work

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Sabbatical applications vary hugely — some require only a form, others need a full written proposal with a project plan, references, or a budget. Knowing what is included shapes the entire plan.
The employer type (academic, corporate, nonprofit) and the specific HR policies in place determine eligibility rules, notice periods, and who holds approval authority.
The intended start date and duration of the sabbatical set the deadline for the application and affect how urgently the user needs to act.
Knowing who needs to approve the request (direct manager, HR, board, department head) determines the sequence of conversations and sign-offs required.
Whether a formal template or process already exists at the organisation, or whether the user must draft something from scratch, changes the first concrete action.
The user's purpose for the sabbatical (research, personal project, travel, health, study) shapes how the application should be framed and what to emphasise to maximise approval chances.
Understanding what a successful outcome looks like — paid vs. unpaid leave, guaranteed job protection, a specific duration — determines what terms the user needs to negotiate or confirm.

gold.taskTitle: Apply for a sabbatical leave from work
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to formally apply for a sabbatical leave from their current employer, which involves understanding eligibility, preparing documentation, and navigating the approval process.

questions.title: What type of organisation do you work for?
questions.description: Is the user in academia, a corporation, a nonprofit, government, etc.? This determines the standard sabbatical policies and processes that apply.

questions.title: What is your intended start date and leave duration?
questions.description: Knowing the target timeline sets the application deadline and urgency of each preparation step.

questions.title: Does your employer have an existing sabbatical application process?
questions.description: Is there a formal form or policy document already in place, or does the user need to create a proposal from scratch?

questions.title: Who has the authority to approve your sabbatical request?
questions.description: Identifying the decision-makers — manager, HR, an executive, a committee — determines the sequence and tone of outreach needed.

questions.title: What is the primary purpose or focus of your sabbatical?
questions.description: The stated reason (research, a personal project, travel, study, health, writing) shapes how the application should be framed to be most persuasive.

questions.title: What does your application need to include or cover?
questions.description: Does the user only need a short request letter, or is a full written proposal with a project plan, timeline, or budget expected?

questions.title: What terms must be secured for this to be a success?
questions.description: Is the user aiming for paid leave, guaranteed job reinstatement, a specific minimum duration, or benefit continuity? Knowing the non-negotiables shapes the negotiation strategy.
